headline: Pelosi reflects on decades-long political career: ‘They made me the villain’
author: Suryatapa Chakraborty

paragraphs.text: Rep. ) reflected on her decades-long political journey this week as she gets ready to retire from Congress in 2027. “They made me the villain,” Pelosi said while discussing how her political career weighed on her family in an interview with “Tea&Vodka” hosted by Ebs Burnough.

“You always have to have a villain; they created me as a villain.” Pelosi also talked about the many difficulties and challenges women face in politics including false narratives, accusations of overspending and portraying women in a “ridiculous” light. “The impression was that women were more ethical and so what they would want to do is to cut that down right away,” Pelosi said.
She is a two-time House Speaker and the only woman to hold the role in American history. Democrats secured a House majority in the 2006 midterm elections for the first time in more than a decade. S.

history. “Now, we have so many women that it’s a little bit different,” she said, however, “it’s still a challenge for women.” Earlier this month, Pelosi announced that she would retire from Congress at the end of the term in January 2027.

In a video addressing her constituents, she said, “With a grateful heart, I look forward to my final year of service as your proud representative.” Over the years, Pelosi has had her notable moments. In 2019, months into her second term as second tenure as Speaker, Pelosi, along with her Democratic colleagues, attended a meeting at the White House with President Trump.

The meeting came after House Democrats, led by Pelosi, launched an impeachment inquiry into Trump. Less than an hour after the meeting started, Pelosi and her colleagues walked out.   During her recent interview, looking back on her career, Pelosi noted, “We really never accomplished what we needed to do … on gun violence,” calling it, “an unfinished business.”
She added that there is a bipartisan community safety bill, but what is needed is background checks, saying, “American people support that but not the Republicans in Congress.”
